head_commit.message:
Avoid sandbox helper in apply_patch approval tests (#28915)

## Summary
This keeps the apply_patch approval tests focused on approval behavior
instead of macOS sandboxed filesystem helper startup.

The changed cases still force patch approval with `UnlessTrusted`, but
use `DangerFullAccess` after approval so the patch write is direct and
cheap. Workspace-write and sandbox-helper behavior remain covered by the
filesystem and apply_patch sandbox tests.

head_commit.message:
[codex] persist fsmonitor status refreshes

Codex passes --no-optional-locks to internal Git commands. This keeps
status from writing a refreshed fsmonitor token after the daemon
restarts, so each background status scans the worktree until another
process updates the index.

Omit the flag from status when Git's built-in fsmonitor is active,
while leaving an inherited GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS override intact. Status
refreshes before trying its optional index lock and continues without
writing if the lock is unavailable. Drive the command to completion
independently of its caller so an acquired lock is committed or rolled
back.

Coalesce status calls per checkout while one is running. Later callers
share its Boolean result instead of starting duplicate scans. Other
internal Git commands retain --no-optional-locks and kill-on-drop.

In an 894,963-entry worktree after a daemon restart, two status runs
with optional locks disabled took 7.45s and 7.01s. With optional locks
enabled, they took 8.01s and 92ms.
